title: Origin validation and loopback listener policy v1
description: The machine surface of docs/security/ORIGIN_AND_LOOPBACK_CONTROLS.md under D-230 and D-231. The document specifies three exact origins, no wildcard, a localhost entry compiled out of the production build, and eight controls on every loopback listener; until this record existed none of that was consumable by a generator, so nothing stopped the deployed behaviour from diverging from the prose. Two surfaces are covered because they fail differently: the public API, whose origin rules are also projected into packages/schemas/openapi-v1.yaml as x-origin-policy, and the loopback listeners, which have no OpenAPI presence at all because they are not the public API. A loopback refusal never crosses the public API wire, so its refusal vocabulary lives here and deliberately not in packages/schemas/reason-codes-v1.json, where every code must bind to a declared API operation.

loopback_controls.description: The eight controls the normative owner requires of every loopback HTTP listener. The list is the control vocabulary; each listener records its own binding for every one of them, so a listener cannot omit a control by omitting a key.

loopback_refusal_codes.description: The refusal vocabulary of the loopback surfaces. These are not API reason codes and must never be added to packages/schemas/reason-codes-v1.json: that registry requires every wire-visible code to bind to a declared OpenAPI operation, and a loopback listener declares none. This list is the reason authority the sandbox conformance suite resolves its expect_reason_code values against.

wildcard_origin.description: Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * is never sent. Recorded as a named value rather than a boolean because a two-valued field written as an enum stays legible inside a digest preimage and inside a diff.

origin_reflection.description: An Origin is never echoed from the request without first being matched against the allowlist. Reflection is the single most common way a three-entry allowlist becomes a wildcard.

state_changing_checks.description: Every applicable check must pass, in the recorded order. Three overlapping controls is deliberate: each covers the others' failure mode.

origin.description: An exact scheme, host and port. No wildcard character may appear.

production_build.description: compiled-out means the entry is absent from the production artifact rather than disabled by configuration. A flag that admits localhost is one environment-variable mistake away from admitting it in production.

unlisted_origin_response.description: A preflight for an origin that is not on the list answers 204 with no Access-Control-* header at all, and the browser blocks the request itself. An error body would tell a probing page whether the origin is known.

applies_to.description: The credential shape the check binds to. cookie-session is the browser path; a bearer-authenticated native request is exempt from the first two checks and from nothing else.

reason_code.description: Resolves in packages/schemas/reason-codes-v1.json. A check the browser enforces carries null, because no server response exists to carry a code.

missing_header.description: What a state-changing cookie-authenticated request with the header absent receives. Every browser sends Origin on POST and DELETE, so its absence means the request did not come from one.

openapiBinding.description: How the policy appears inside the OpenAPI document, so a client or middleware generator reading only that document sees the same rule.

required_on_security_scheme.description: Every operation whose security includes this scheme declares the Origin parameter, and no operation that does not include it may declare one. csrfToken already marks exactly the state-changing cookie-authenticated set under PF-039, so the origin arm binds to the same set by construction rather than by a second hand-maintained list.

preflight_routing.description: Preflight is answered by the edge before routing, not per operation. Declaring an options operation on every path would claim per-operation preflight routing that no CORS implementation performs, so the response component is declared once and referenced by the extension.

closes.description: The attack this control closes and the others do not. A control that closes nothing the others do not is redundant and should be removed rather than recorded.

authentication.description: none is a recorded fact and not an omission. The adapter-one OTLP receiver is an unauthenticated localhost endpoint that any local process can POST at, and no loopback control changes that: a local process running as the participant is indistinguishable from the participant.

input_trust.description: untrusted means the listener treats its request bodies as adversarial input regardless of who reached the socket. Origin controls stop a web page from reaching the listener; they are not a substitute for input validation and are never cited as one.

controls.description: One binding per control in loopback_controls, keyed by control_id. A listener that cannot apply a control records not-applicable with the reason rather than omitting the key, so an absent control is always visible.

host_allowlist.description: The exact Host values the listener accepts. This is the control that defeats DNS rebinding: a rebound request still carries the attacker's name in Host, because the browser sends the name it was given and not the address it resolved to.

cors_headers.description: A loopback surface sends no Access-Control-Allow-Origin, no Access-Control-Allow-Credentials, and answers no preflight with an allow. There is no legitimate cross-origin consumer of a local control API.
